target_customer: Corporate sales and deal teams that manage contracts, approvals and signatures
problem: Contracts get stuck in email chains with no visibility, versions or workflow.

founders.name: Eli Rubel
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch at Disrupt NY 2013

founders.name: Justin Thiele
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch at Disrupt NY 2013

founders.name: Henry Liu
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; the YC page names different people from TechCrunch

founders.name: Brandon Paton
founders.background_notes: YC page lists as founder of Localize

competitors.name: HelloSign
competitors.what: Free digital signature service from HelloFax; overlaps only on signing

competitors.name: DocuSign
competitors.what: E-signature incumbent named as HelloSign's competitor

technical_complexity.rationale: Document import, versioning, approvals and signature collection with Box, Dropbox and Gmail integrations is standard SaaS work.

defensibility.rationale: Contract data creates some lock in, but signing vendors could add workflow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: FPX, a sales software firm, bought Glider in April 2014 for an undisclosed price.

market_need_then: Co-founder Eli Rubel said Glider aimed to do for contracts what Salesforce did for the sales funnel; the evidence of demand is the 1M USD seed and the FPX purchase.

branding.name_origin: Glider was formerly named Superbly; no source says why it was renamed.

brand_strength.rationale: Name change before TechStars Seattle Demo Day in November 2012 and no sourced brand effects; the name collides with later unrelated products named Glider.

pivots.from: Superbly (earlier a photo album startup, Tell It In 10)

outcome_analysis: Glider raised about 1.3M to 1.4M USD, launched at TechCrunch Disrupt NY in April 2013 and was acquired by FPX a year later. Silicon Florist and an investor quote call it a good exit for Portland Seed Fund, but the price is undisclosed and the team did not raise a Series A, so it ended as a soft landing.
notes: YC page lists Henry Liu, Brandon Paton and John Marbach, while TechCrunch names Eli Rubel and Justin Thiele; the sources conflict and the match between the YC Glider and the Portland Glider is by name, domain glider.io and description. Website glider.io redirects to a domain sale page. The 2012 350K round rests on a single database (Seedtable) and Seedtable also lists Primera Capital as lead of the 2013 round, conflicting with Silicon Florist and TechCrunch (True Ventures). Aggregator totals range 1.03M to 1.4M USD. as_of is the April 2013 launch; competitor sources are from Aug 2012 and overlap only on signing. Founder education and employers not found. The YC directory marks the company Inactive because it was acquired; exit.type acquisition is correct and the conflict is only the directory label.
